### Summary

The numerics switches and the YAML options can be combined, but not every combination has a test. The table in this
section says, for each combination a registered test exercises, which test it is and what it asserts, so a reader
can tell a combination that is checked from one that merely runs.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Maps switch combinations to registered assertions.

**Data.** CTest registrations and child-process arms in; coverage rows out.

**Placement.** Match the registration to the arm before interpreting a result.

**Activation.** Choose an explicit row and sanitize inherited switch values.

**Guarantee / limits.** A setup guard is not an accuracy test; registration is not execution.

**Evidence.** Tests below, @tbl-ch12-matrix-tests; solver ctests were not run.
:::

Table key: WB, XC, FC, MC and RE are the switches defined at the chapter opening.
`<b>` is the lower-case build suffix; "child" means a fresh process per arm,
and "CTest" means the registration sets the variable.

### Derivation

Coverage is a relation between a configuration and a test assertion, not a probability or an accuracy
estimate. A row is supported only when both the registration and the test's actual arm agree; a guard
assertion supports setup behaviour, not an error norm. Check line `[C11]` states the relation as a table:
support is the conjunction of registration and arm over its four combinations, and of the four (assertion
kind, claim kind) pairs exactly one is unsupported, a guard assertion offered for an error norm
[check `src/snapy_report/ch12/checks/configuration_check.py`, output
`src/snapy_report/ch12/checks/configuration_check.out`].

### Numerical method

First select a build that contains the required entries, then establish the import provenance, sanitize the
numerics switches, and launch the named arm. Compare the invariant that the gravity-work mode selects: energy
plus corrected potential energy for `face` with RE on, energy plus plain potential energy otherwise. Record
CPU or CUDA and the rank count with every measured result. The dependency figure shows the logical constraints
of the switches, not measured performance.

### Code

**How to use it.** Pick one row, inspect its registration, then execute its exact test name in a compatible
build. For the WB seam row in a Release build:

```bash
env -u SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT SNAP_WB_REF4=0 SNAP_X1_MASS_COVARIANCE=0 \
  SNAP_FLUX_COVARIANCE=0 SNAP_GRAVITY_WORK_RADIAL_EXACT=0 \
  ctest --test-dir build -R '^test_x1_seam_split_wb_ref4.release$' --output-on-failure
```

CTest overrides WB for this registered arm; the other values prevent inherited study flags from changing it.
`SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` is removed with `-u`, not set to `0`: the arm asserts that the variable is unset, and an
unset variable is the off state it checks. `-u` comes before the assignments, which the `env` of macOS requires.
This row supplies its own deck, so no extra YAML is needed. A missing entry, disabled arm or empty selection is
not evidence. Setup refusals constrain configuration only, and cannot certify an error norm.

The `seam_arm` registration in {{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt >}} selects the environment and assertion:

```cmake
seam_arm(_wb_ref4 "SNAP_WB_REF4=1"
         wb_ref4_flag_at_the_seam_split_matches_one_block)
```

The first argument supplies the name suffix, the second sets WB, and the third selects the gtest case.
The coverage relation of `[C11]` requires both this registration and the executed arm to match the claim.
XC must remain off in a WB-off control because XC implies WB.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| all entries in the matrix | registered assertions only | see the individual scheme tables | no runtime results in this chapter |
| `configuration_check.py` `[C11]` (report check) | the registration/arm support relation | exact symbolic or Boolean equality | the independent check |

: Source assertions, not new solver measurements. {#tbl-ch12-matrix-tests}

No snapy runtime test is executed for this chapter. CUDA and multi-rank entries describe registration only.
The independent checks and their outputs are catalogued in @sec-ch15-ch12-tests.

The independent report check verifies the registration/arm support relation in `[C11]`.[^ch12-matrix-run]
It models the stated contract; it does not execute the compiled solver.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
Numerical MC behaviour, XC with face work or RE, XC together with FC, WB or XC on gnomonic grids, WB with RE off
under face work, FC across MPI ranks, and the wider simultaneous combinations have no registered evidence.
WB together with FC and RE has a registered order oracle; an all-flags combination is not thereby covered.

The complete switch inventory is this section.
:::
